dedupe_keys.name: lamp argentine space weather laboratory data and products

description: LAMP, the Argentine space weather laboratory at the University of Buenos Aires, publishes operational space weather data and products in Spanish. Its pages cover solar activity (SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph images of the last four days, SDO HMI magnetograms of the last seven days with active region numbers, and GOES-16 X-ray flux with flare classes), the interplanetary medium, the geomagnetic field, the ionosphere, cosmic rays, the radiation environment, the Antarctic region, forecasts, alerts and bulletins, each with a plain-language explanation of what the data shows. Access is free and public; many plots come from NASA and NOAA sources that are credited on the pages, and no licence is stated. Caveats: the site combines external data with local products, and the archive depth of each product is not given on the page read. Coverage is Argentina, with global solar context. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather for power grids, GNSS and HF communications in South America; related records are SCiESMEX of Mexico and the BRIN SWIFtS service.
